title: Largest Combination With Bitwise AND Greater Than Zero
statement:
You are given an array `candidates` of positive integers. A combination is any non-empty group of elements taken from distinct positions of `candidates` (equal values at different positions may both be picked). The bitwise AND of a combination is what you get by AND-ing all of its numbers together; a combination of one number has that number as its AND.

Return the size of the biggest combination whose bitwise AND is greater than 0.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every combination is exponential. The key observation is that an AND is above 0 exactly when some bit is set in **every** chosen number. So pick a bit: all numbers that have that bit can go into one combination together, and its AND keeps that bit. The answer is the largest such group over all bit positions. Since `10^7 < 2^24`, only 24 bits matter.

## Approach

1. Start `best` at 0.
2. For each `bit` from 0 to 23, set `count` to 0.
3. Walk through every `value` and add 1 to `count` when `value` has that bit set.
4. After the walk, `count` is the size of the biggest combination sharing that bit; keep the maximum in `best`.
5. Return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`candidates = [16, 17, 71, 62, 12, 24, 14]`. Bit 0 (value 1) is in 17 and 71: count 2. Bit 1 (2) is in 71, 62, 14: count 3. Bit 2 (4) is in 71, 62, 12, 14: count 4. Bit 3 (8) is in 62, 12, 24, 14: count 4. Bit 4 (16) is in 16, 17, 62, 24: count 4. Bit 5 (32) is in 62: 1. Bit 6 (64) is in 71: 1. Higher bits count 0. The largest count, and the answer, is `4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(24 · n): each of the 24 bits scans the array once.
- Space: O(1): only a few counters.

## Pitfalls

- Do not search for the best combination directly; the largest one is always "everyone with bit b" for some b.
- Cover all 24 bits: values up to 10^7 use bit 23.
- Count positions, not distinct values: `[8, 8]` gives 2.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `best` | largest combination size found so far |
| `bit` | the bit position being tested |
| `count` | how many candidates have `bit` set |
| `value` | the candidate being examined |

narration.2: No combination has been measured yet, so the best size starts at 0.
narration.3: Try each of the 24 bit positions that a value up to 10^7 can use.
narration.4: Start a fresh count of numbers carrying this bit.
narration.6: Shift the bit down to position 0 and test whether it is 1.
narration.7: This number has the bit, so it can join the combination for this bit.
narration.10: All numbers sharing this bit form a valid combination; keep the largest such size.
narration.12: The biggest group sharing any single bit is the answer.
